newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAS estimates strike cost at 800 million yen.
newsitem.headline: JAS estimates strike cost at 800 million yen.

text.p: Japan Air System Co Ltd (JAS) said on Friday that a one-day strike on Wednesday would cost it 800 million yen in lost revenues.
The carrier has also been in the red by more than one billion yen per month since April due to intensified domestic competition that led to lower domestic air fares, a JAS spokeswoman said.
"For us, this (the financial impact of the strike) is certainly big," she said.
JAS said in May it expects a 500 million yen parent current profit for the year ending in March 1998 against an actual 276 million yen in parent current profit a year earlier.

Asked whether the financial damage from the strike would affect the carrier's earnings forecast, the JAS spokesman said: "We are still in the first quarter, so we would like to put more effort into sales and turn the tide."
JAS is Japan's third-largest carrier and operates mostly domestic flights.

The strike halted 92 percent of the carrier's domestic flights and affected 44,000 passengers after talks broke down between JAS's two labour unions and company management on employees' summer bonuses and other issues.
